transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-01 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Lynwood Head of Platform), Ben Richards (Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (Security), Ethan Cole (DevOps), Zoe Kim (Legal)

Summary:
Customer evaluating Redwood Private deployment behind their VPC. Primary concerns: region restrictions (EU/US separation), private endpoints vs peering, egress/BYOC KMS for PHI, audit logs/SOC2 mapping, latency targets for inference (tail p50/p95), and cost delta between Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Topics: network topology, private endpoints & DNS, transit gateway and peering, KMS/HSM integration, audit log retention, latency SLAs, fallback strategies, onboarding timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: All right hey everyone thanks for joining. quick roll call: i m avery chen from Redwood, samir is also here, samir you wanna wave hi?
[00:07] Samir Patel: yeah hi everybody, thanks for having us.
[00:10] Maya Ortiz: hey thanks avery, appreciate it. we scheduled a tight window so we ll jump in.
[00:15] Avery Chen: perfect. ben, priya — do you want to intro yourselves briefly?
[00:19] Ben Richards: sure. ben richards, cloud architect — i m the one who will be doing the peering and transit gateway config with our infra team.
[00:24] Priya Singh: priya singh, security — i m focused on data residency, encryption, SOC 2 scope.
[00:29] Ethan Cole: ethan cole, devops — i m responsible for network ops and perf testing.
[00:33] Zoe Kim: zoe from legal just listening in for procurement flags.
[00:36] Avery Chen: great. quick agenda: we wanted to understand your current networking posture and constraints, walk through our private deployment options (private endpoints, peering, dedicated hosts), and map out next steps/workshop. sound good?
[00:44] Maya Ortiz: sounds right. we re aiming to host PHI workloads so we ve got strict region and key management needs, and minimal internet egress if possible.
[00:52] Samir Patel: quick clarify — when you say PHI, do you also have HIPAA business associate agreements in place or required?
[00:57] Priya Singh: yes we ll need a BAA and we re expecting full support for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM), also audit logs that we can ingest into our SIEM.
[01:07] Samir Patel: understood, we ve done BAAs and KMS integrations; we ll cover the audit log export options.
[01:12] Ben Richards: on the networking side — we re multi-region: us-east and eu-west are our production regions, but strict separation for eu workloads — data must not egress to us. so we need Redwood to guarantee region pinning.
[01:25] Avery Chen: yes region pinning is doable. for Private deployments we can instantiate a control plane in your chosen region and keep inference nodes in-region. note: for Dedicated we sometimes route to a central control plane — we ll call out the difference.
[01:36] Ben Richards: okay, can you explain the connectivity patterns — private endpoint vs VPC peering vs transit-gateway? what s easiest to manage with our existing transit setup?
[01:44] Samir Patel: sure. high level: three common patterns we recommend depending on scale and your transit topology.
[01:49] Samir Patel: pattern one is private endpoints (privatelink style) where Redwood exposes an ENI/private endpoint in your VPC and you route to it — minimizes cross-account peering and is often simplest for constrained security teams.
[02:00] Samir Patel: pattern two is VPC peering — direct VPC-to-VPC connectivity, lower latency but doesn t scale well with many accounts; also depends on overlapping CIDRs.
[02:10] Samir Patel: pattern three is transit-gateway or equivalent where you attach Redwood s VPC to your transit for centralized routing; this suits orgs using TGW for shared services.
[02:19] Ben Richards: we do use a transit gateway in us-east and eu-west; so transit attachments might be easiest. but our security team prefers endpoints where possible since it s more explicit.
[02:28] Priya Singh: endpoints are preferred because we can apply tighter IAM and endpoint policies; peering will require more ACL management across accounts. also need to confirm IP scopes — we re using 10.0.0.0/8 range across the org.
[02:40] Ethan Cole: our NAT egress is locked down too, we have strict egress rules — ideally inference nodes should not require outbound internet access except for control plane heartbeat.
[02:49] Samir Patel: that s fine — Redwood Private supports no-Internet egress modes. control plane communication can be via private link or via a managed proxy in your network. we also support egress through a customer-managed NAT if you prefer.
[03:01] Maya Ortiz: how do you handle DNS resolution for private endpoints? we run internal resolving and split-horizon DNS. will Redwood provide hostname records?
[03:09] Samir Patel: we provide instructions to create private hosted zone entries; for Private deployments we can publish internal FQDNs to your zone, or you can point specific records to the endpoint IPs. split-horizon is common.
[03:19] Ben Richards: ping latency is important — our inference loop needs p95 under 120ms for smaller models; can you provide perf profiles from eu-west?
[03:27] Avery Chen: yes we have model-level perf bench sheets. we ll include p50/p95 numbers for the models you re evaluating. but keep in mind that adding a transit hop or firewall inspection can add 10-30ms.
[03:38] Ethan Cole: ok that s acceptable. what about KV cache locality? we re sensitive to cold-start token costs.
[03:44] Samir Patel: we maintain local KV cache per region — in Private deployments the cache is co-located with inference nodes so latency penalty is minimized.
[03:50] Priya Singh: KMS — can we bring our keys? do you store any plaintext?
[03:55] Samir Patel: customers can bring keys via AWS KMS or a compatible HSM; Redwood will encrypt model cache and at-rest storage with your keys. we don t persist raw customer data outside encrypted storage; we can provide key rotation workflows.
[04:06] Maya Ortiz: good. audit logs — we need request-level logs and token usage for billing reconciliation and audits. can you stream logs to our S3 or SIEM?
[04:13] Samir Patel: yes we can stream structured audit logs to an S3 bucket or push to your Kinesis/CloudWatch/Splunk endpoint. we also support syslog forwarding for onprem SIEMs.
[04:22] Ben Richards: are these logs redacted by default? PHI concerns — we d prefer tokens stripped before sending.
[04:28] Samir Patel: by default logs include request metadata, timestamps, model used; payloads can be redacted or masked per configuration. we can show the templates in the workshop.
[04:36] Zoe Kim: any legal flags about data processing agreements for cross-border? we re particularly strict about eu subjects data staying in eu.
[04:42] Avery Chen: we can support region isolation — we d host EU workloads in eu-west and never replicate to US hosts for that tenancy. we ll outline the deployment topology in the runbook.
[04:52] Maya Ortiz: from an onboarding perspective, how long does provisioning take for private?
[04:56] Samir Patel: provisioning depends — if you re using private endpoints and attaching to our pre-provisioned private nodes, it can be days. For fully dedicated on-prem/private within your VPC we schedule a network workshop then 2-4 weeks for capacity provisioning and validation.
[05:08] Ethan Cole: what about burst capacity — we have spiky inference. can Redwood autoscale within the VPC?
[05:14] Samir Patel: yes autoscaling works for Dedicated/Private modes. If you want absolute control, we can provision reserved nodes and enable burst queues to a shared pool. this is part of the Dedicated offering with an enterprise contract.
[05:25] Ben Richards: okay, cost question — difference between Hosted and Private for our usage (mostly 8k-12k small inference qps, mixed models).
[05:33] Avery Chen: we ll send a detailed cost model but quick answer: Hosted is cheapest to start but you trade control and region isolation. Dedicated reduces unit cost at scale and offers reserved capacity; Private (VPC deployed) adds networking and egress considerations and there s an integration/operational fee. we ll quantify in the pricing doc.
[05:47] Priya Singh: we ll need SOC 2 and ISO attestation docs for procurement. do you have a standard package?
[05:52] Avery Chen: yes SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts available under NDA. we ll add them to the security packet in the next email.
[05:59] Maya Ortiz: great. on network specifics — here s our constraints: 10.10.0.0/16 for prod eu-west, 10.20.0.0/16 for prod us-east, transit gw in each region, strict egress, and no public IPs assigned to inference nodes. is that supported?
[06:14] Samir Patel: yes — private deployments can live in your private subnets and we can avoid public IP assignments. we ll need your subnet CIDRs and route table attachments to propose exact peering/endpoint config.
[06:24] Ben Richards: we also use internal load balancers for other services — can Redwood speak to ALB/NLB requirements?
[06:30] Samir Patel: for private endpoints we typically recommend NLB in front of the private endpoint if you need cross-AZ resilience. for traffic coming through TGW the recommendation varies — we ll include diagrams.
[06:39] Ethan Cole: what about IP whitelisting and egress IP ranges — procurement wants fixed IP ranges for firewall rules.
[06:45] Avery Chen: for Private we can provide static egress IP ranges per region when traffic exits via Redwood managed NAT, or you can force egress through your own NAT. we ll capture your preference in the runbook.
[06:57] Priya Singh: incident response — how do we get alerted on model regressions or anomalous traffic?
[07:02] Samir Patel: the Redwood Console supports alerting; we can forward to your PagerDuty and include a runbook for escalations. analytics include token-level cost, latency, error rates.
[07:11] Ben Richards: we re also interested in canary and rollback — we do model rollouts and need to test new quantized variants in region before full switch.
[07:18] Samir Patel: we support canary routing and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if latency degrades. those are configured in rollout policy and can be bound to route/tenant.
[07:27] Maya Ortiz: legal question — does Redwood persist prompts for more than 30 days by default? we have retention requirements.
[07:34] Avery Chen: default retention is 30 days for Hosted telemetry, but for Private we can configure retention windows longer or shorter; we can also disable payload persistence entirely depending on your compliance profile.
[07:45] Zoe Kim: any encryption-in-transit clarifications — we d like mTLS between our services and the endpoint.
[07:51] Samir Patel: mTLS is supported for endpoint connections; we can provide client certificates or integrate with your CA.
[07:57] Ben Richards: one more — egress inspection by our DLP tooling is done inline at our firewall; will that break the inference traffic?
[08:03] Samir Patel: often inspection at lower levels is fine, but if content is rewritten it could break the protocol. best practice is to allow TLS passthrough for inference traffic and inspect metadata only. we ll document exact ports and protocols.
[08:16] Avery Chen: okay i want to pause and outline immediate deliverables: samir will prepare a security & network runbook and draft architecture diagrams for both private endpoint and transit-gateway attachment patterns; i ll follow up with pricing and compliance artifacts; maya to share topology.
[08:31] Maya Ortiz: yep we ll do that — i ll push a topo diagram and a matrix of data residency rules.
[08:35] Ethan Cole: we d also like a short perf test plan — minimal steps we run from our side to validate latency.
[08:41] Samir Patel: we have a perf checklist and a lightweight load generator; we ll send that as part of the workshop kit.
[08:47] Ben Richards: timeline wise — we re hoping to have a POC by end of Q2. is that realistic?
[08:52] Avery Chen: yes if we start the network workshop this month and you provide the VPC details, we can aim for a 6-8 week POC that includes setup, validation, and a small production pilot.
[08:59] Priya Singh: procurement will want clear SLAs and a fall-back plan — what does Redwood offer for downtime/region failure?
[09:06] Samir Patel: we offer cross-region fallback policies for Dedicated; for Private we can run a secondary replica in another region but that requires network prep and data replication strategy. fallback can be configured to a hosted model in a different region if you accept cross-border failover; otherwise you can have standby capacity in-region.
[09:22] Avery Chen: good question for tradeoffs — we ll enumerate options in the runbook.
[09:25] Maya Ortiz: any gotchas we should prepare for from our infra side?
[09:29] Samir Patel: common ones: overlapping CIDRs (we need unique ranges), missing route propagation on TGW, restrictive NACLs blocking health checks, and RBAC sync issues if you want SSO mapped to roles.
[09:39] Ethan Cole: RBAC — does Redwood support mapping SAML groups to roles?
[09:44] Samir Patel: yep SAML/SCIM sync, SSO and fine-grained RBAC supported for Private and Dedicated.
[09:50] Zoe Kim: procurement will also ask for indemnity clauses and breach notification windows. we have standard timelines — 24 to 72 hours depending on severity.
[09:58] Avery Chen: we can discuss breach notification in the contract — we re used to 48-hour windows for critical incidents.
[10:04] Ben Richards: okay that s super helpful. couple final items — do you have a template for the security questionnaire we can pre-fill?
[10:10] Avery Chen: yes we ll provide the security questionnaire answers and an editable template.
[10:13] Maya Ortiz: thanks.
[10:15] Samir Patel: one more note on routing: if you prefer least-privilege connectivity, private endpoints scoped to specific subnets plus IAM policy gives the tightest control; if you need cross-account scale TGW is more operationally efficient.
[10:29] Maya Ortiz: that makes sense. let s lock in the workshop week of the 11th.
[10:33] Avery Chen: perfect — i ll send a doodle for availability and the pre-req checklist.
[10:37] Zoe Kim: legal will review the BAA template before we sign.
[10:40] Avery Chen: understood. any other questions?
[10:43] Ben Richards: none from me.
[10:45] Priya Singh: no.
[10:46] Maya Ortiz: great thanks everyone.
[10:48] Avery Chen: thanks all, we ll follow up with the runbook, pricing, and SOC docs. talk soon.

Recap (auto):
- Customer goals: deploy Redwood in private VPCs for PHI, strict EU/US separation, customer-managed KMS, no public IPs, minimal egress.
- Recommended next steps: provide topology, schedule SE-led workshop, share security artifacts and pricing.

Attachments referenced: "Redwood_private_deploy_runbook.pdf" (to be shared), "Perf_checklist.xlsx" (to be shared), SOC2/ISO artifacts (NDA).
